canonical: track-me-web/tests/fixtures — copy to each client, same as group-status-vectors.json
note: SCOPE_1.8.7 §6.1.3 scenario 12a and §6.1.2 scenario 10b — what the app may infer from a rider's own history. Scenario 12 was CUT for inferring a routine and acting on it; 12a keeps the inference and hands the decision back. That distinction only holds if the suggestion is withheld whenever it would be a guess, so most of these vectors are about REFUSING to suggest. A platform that suggests where the other stays quiet is the app appearing to watch more closely on one phone than the other.

constants._day_note: ISO-8601 weekday: 1 = Monday … 7 = Sunday. NOT java.util.Calendar's or Foundation's numbering, both of which make Sunday 1 — a vector written against either would be a trap for the other platform.
constants._share_note: A rider who rides every day has no usual day. 30% is roughly double what a uniform week gives any single day.

suggest_slot.note: Four of five rides on Saturday, three of them at 08:00. The 09:00 outlier does not move the hour because the modal hour wins outright.

suggest_slot.description: four rides is not yet a history
suggest_slot.note: A perfect pattern, refused for lack of evidence. The floor is deliberately above the point where a pattern becomes visible, because the cost of a confidently wrong suggestion is higher than the cost of an empty form.

suggest_slot.description: rides every day of the week
suggest_slot.note: One ride on each day. There is no usual day to suggest, and picking Monday because it sorts first would be the app inventing a routine. Note the hour is unambiguous and it still refuses — the day gate runs first for a reason.

suggest_slot.description: a dominant day carried by a single ride
suggest_slot.note: Five rides, five different days, so the modal day has exactly one ride. Both the share gate and the two-ride gate refuse it.

suggest_slot.description: a tie between two days breaks to the earlier weekday
suggest_slot.note: Tuesday and Saturday both have two rides. The tie breaks deterministically rather than by map order — a suggestion that changes between two runs over identical history is one nobody can trust.

suggest_slot.description: the hour comes only from the dominant day's rides
suggest_slot.note: 19:00 is the most common hour overall, but Saturday's rides are at 08:00. Averaging across the week would suggest an hour the rider has never once ridden at on the day being suggested.

suggest_slot.description: the persona comes from the dominant day too
suggest_slot.note: RUN is the more frequent persona overall, but the Saturday slot being suggested is a cycling slot. A reminder that names the wrong activity is worse than one that names none.
A fresh install gets an empty form, not a default dressed up as a suggestion.

typical_active_minutes.description: odd count takes the middle value
even count averages the middle pair, rounding down
typical_active_minutes.note: (31 + 40) / 2 = 35.5, truncated to 35. Under-promising is the correct direction of error for scenario 10b.

typical_active_minutes.description: a forgotten six-hour ride does not move the median
typical_active_minutes.note: The exact reason this is a median and not a mean. Scenario 4 exists because rides like the last one happen, so the statistic feeding scenario 10b has to shrug them off — a mean of 96 would promise a level the rider will not reach today.

typical_active_minutes.description: a persona with one ride falls back to the whole history
typical_active_minutes.note: One cycle ride is not a cycling history. Refusing to answer would silently disable 10b on exactly the first ride of a new activity, where a new level is most likely.

typical_active_minutes.description: a persona with enough of its own history uses it
typical_active_minutes.note: Two cycle rides clear the floor, so cycling is measured against cycling rather than being dragged down by the runs.

start_button_proximity.description: a typical ride crosses the threshold

start_button_proximity.note: Inclusive at the boundary. A rider whose median ride is exactly the gap does cross it half the time, and the sentence is a prediction rather than a promise.

start_button_proximity.description: further away than this rider usually goes
start_button_proximity.note: The honest sentence here is 'this one does not, quite'. Saying the encouraging one instead is how a prediction feature stops being believed.

start_button_proximity.description: a short rider is not told a distant level is close
start_button_proximity.note: The same 20-minute gap that produces a line for a 40-minute rider produces nothing here. This is the whole point of bounding it by the rider's own history rather than a constant.

start_button_proximity.description: a first-time rider gets no prediction
start_button_proximity.note: No history means no basis. Inventing a default ride length would be the app guessing about a stranger and then telling them what it guessed.

start_button_proximity.description: a blank level name is not a level
